name: architect
does: Traces the existing system, generates competing usage-first type and module sketches through arena, synthesizes one, then implements and redesigns if recurring friction disproves the sketch.
why: A substantial pipeline redesign may benefit from competing module sketches. Most current work is narrower experimentation, where your existing design tools and a small implementation are a better starting point.
caveat: Invoke for a substantial pipeline redesign, not each small function. It proceeds to implementation by default; request a checkpoint for design-only work. Requires how/arena and adaptation of Cursor model/tool assumptions.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: arena
does: Runs isolated parallel candidates, cross-judges them against a rubric, selects a base, grafts useful ideas from the others and verifies the synthesis.
why: You repeatedly ask for genuinely different ideas and visual variants. Comparing a small set and combining the strongest parts can improve the result directly, although your existing maker/verifier/judge process already covers much of it.
caveat: Use when several plausible approaches deserve comparison. Its identical candidate prompt does not guarantee the distinct forms the user requests; specify those in the framing. Adapt unavailable models and cap resource use on the MacBook.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: automate-me
does: Mines scoped recent transcripts, checks recurring preferences with the user and authors or updates a personal, explicitly invoked mode skill.
why: Your repeated prompt refinements suggest value in a short personal workflow. Its benefit depends on replacing repeated instructions and unnecessary steps, not creating a larger personal rule bundle.
caveat: This creates a working-style skill, not scheduled task automation. Adapt Cursor transcript paths/create-skill tools to Codex and validate preferences across a broader sample; the 60 summaries and six detailed chats are not a complete profile.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: blast-radius
does: Reviews consequences beyond the diff, identifies the key safety assumption, and attempts to prove it by running real code rather than listing hypothetical risks.
why: Useful for a high-impact evaluator or data-filter change, but not a routine extra review for every task. Existing review and integration checks reduce the added benefit.
caveat: Best before evaluator, data-filtering or shared-format changes merge. One proved safety fact is not comprehensive correctness; retain the existing regression and integration checks. Wider changes can invoke arena and increase cost.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: bro
does: Restates the previous assistant message more simply and concisely without jargon.
why: A quick simpler restatement can help when an agent's answer is opaque. It is a low-effort tool, but a normal request for plain language may achieve the same result and it cannot fill missing research.
caveat: Invoke after an opaque answer. It does not research, verify, teach interactively or explain missing background.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: create-verification-skill
does: Inspects a repo, creates a project-specific launch/health-check/drive/evidence/cleanup skill and feature map, then executes one real feature end to end to prove the generated instructions.
why: You explicitly said this skill would not be beneficial. The original audit confused your need for reliable results with a need to create and maintain another verification skill; keep existing checks and deprioritize this addition.
caveat: Deprioritized by your feedback. A useful verification habit does not establish that authoring a dedicated verification skill is worthwhile. The 2/10 benefit score is a revised editorial estimate, not a score you supplied.
revisionBasis: Direct user feedback; numeric estimate assigned by assistant.

name: figure-it-out
does: Designs a bespoke workflow for large or unusual work, establishes a falsifiable completion predicate and baseline, runs small measured experiments and maintains a linked decision trail.
why: Your open-ended research and optimization questions need a route from an idea to a useful experiment. This can help choose the next informative action; use a shortened version so its orchestration does not become another project.
caveat: Reserve for ambitious multi-part changes where a narrower workflow does not suffice. It brings dependencies on poteto-mode principles, architect/arena and show-me-your-work; avoid importing all of that for a small experiment.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: how
does: Traces a subsystem from real source into an architectural explanation, optionally followed by independent architecture critics and a filtered verdict.
why: Tracing the real code can directly answer how your sampler, evaluator or masked-completion pipeline works. Request plain language and skip the optional critic panel unless an architectural decision needs it.
caveat: This explains code for a senior-engineer audience, not papers or beginner concepts. Explicitly request plain language when needed. Even the simple path delegates once, and critique adds a model panel; adapt this overhead and the Cursor APIs.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: interrogate
does: Gives the same intent, code and rubric to multiple model reviewers, then synthesizes consensus, disagreements and prioritized findings without applying fixes.
why: Several reviewers can help with a consequential code change. It adds cost and duplicated judgments to your existing review tools, and does not address your recurring request to clarify an idea or prompt.
caveat: This is code review, not a replacement for grilling the user about a prompt. Model agreement is not independent proof; validate findings. Its default model slugs and Cursor Task syntax need replacement in Codex.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: maintain-verification-skill
does: Audits every feature in an existing verification skill against source and live behavior, corrects only its documentation/harness/map, and reports clean, changed or blocked.
why: If creating a dedicated verification skill is not useful to you, maintaining one has little current value. Reconsider only if you later rely on such a skill and it demonstrably saves work.
caveat: Conditional on first finding or creating a verification skill with a feature map. Every mapped feature gets a live exercise, so keep the map bounded. Product regressions are reported, not fixed by this workflow.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: no-comments
does: Runs the Comment Sicko agent to delete comments outside a narrow exception list, then fixes accepted code-shape findings and offers structural encodings of constraints.
why: Deleting explanatory comments does not directly support your research or learning goals and can erase useful constraints. Avoid its broad cleanup behavior.
caveat: Not a read-only review. Ambiguous keep cases are deleted, and constraint comments can be deleted even when the user declines the proposed encoding, with the constraint reported open. Avoid as a default, especially in research code.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: poteto-mode
does: Applies a comprehensive personal workflow with mandatory principle reads, delegation, architecture exploration, verification, prose rules and task-specific playbooks.
why: A complete borrowed mode adds mandatory architecture, delegation, review and cleanup steps that may not improve your outcomes. Your feedback favors selecting useful pieces rather than adopting another person's full process.
caveat: Prefer selected leaf workflows or a personal automate-me result. This mode mandates architect for code crossing a function boundary, no-comments before review, and dependencies such as Cursor agents, cursor-team-kit and Graphite. Its broad permission for external actions does not replace the user's authorization or host rules.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: recall
does: Reconstructs recent scoped working context from chat history and shared records, checks artifacts against live state, and returns a compact current-status brief and next move.
why: You move between many related chats and ask agents to reuse established project decisions. A short, scoped context recovery can reduce repeated explanations; much of the mechanism already exists in your tools.
caveat: Use before resuming work, not as the daily-blog summarizer: the skill explicitly distinguishes those tasks. Adapt Cursor history paths and shared-record tools, and report exactly which time range/workspaces were searched.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: reflect
does: Reviews the active conversation through judgment, tooling and divergent lenses, synthesizes durable lessons into proposed skill edits or structural backlog items, and applies approved skill changes.
why: A competition retrospective or repeated agent failure can justify reflection. Routine skill edits, backlog entries and multiple review lenses would impose maintenance without an established payoff.
caveat: Use after a consequential correction, not every conversation. It requires approval for skill edits, but separately instructs automatic backlog filing; disable/adapt external filing unless authorized. Avoid treating a one-session preference as a universal rule.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.

name: setup-pstack
does: Detects available subagent models, lets the user choose models for Pstack roles, and writes a Cursor always-applied model-override rule.
why: This configures Pstack model roles for Cursor. You are auditing in Codex and have not decided to adopt the bundle, so setup itself currently provides little benefit.
caveat: Useful only after deciding to run Pstack in a compatible host or port its configuration mechanism. Confirm real available model IDs; do not assume the pinned defaults or Cursor rule path work in Codex.
revisionBasis: Reassessed using the user's feedback as a preference for useful outcomes over additional process; this broader preference is an inference.
